groups.name: The Alcur Hospital
lore: The Alcur Hospital is a medical practice focused on curing anomalous ailments, based within extradimensional space. Led by a multiversal deity named Dr. Alcur, the group cooperates with the Global Occult Coalition to assist anyone in need of treatment, operating in an unknown and potentially infinite number of alternate dimensions. Many of the staff employed are anomalous in nature, with therians being particularly prevalent.

Despite their benevolent and cooperative nature, the Alcur Hospital disrupts the operations of the Foundation in every reality in which they operate, due to conflicting beliefs with regard to how humanity should be protected. This has included deliberately reversing the effects of amnestics, protesting against the Foundation’s treatment of sapient anomalies, and breaking the Veil if they deem it necessary to save lives.

Staff of the Alcur Hospital are to be approached with caution, as its security personnel are trained in advanced ontokinetics and equipped with advanced eigenmechs, which they use both within the hospital's own dimension and outside of it. This training and armament is always used with great restraint, and there have been no recorded casualties from hostile interactions with the Alcur Hospital.
Foundation personnel are prohibited from seeking treatment from the Alcur Hospital, unless specifically authorised due to operational necessity or for undercover operations.
groups.purpose: An extradimensional medical practice, led by the multiversal deity Dr. Alcur, that exists to cure anomalous ailments for anyone in need.
groups.gear: Security personnel trained in advanced ontokinetics and equipped with advanced eigenmechs.
gearQuotes: Staff of the Alcur Hospital are to be approached with caution, as its security personnel are trained in advanced ontokinetics and equipped with advanced eigenmechs, which they use both within the hospital's own dimension and outside of it.

groups.name: Alexylva University
lore: Overview: Very little is known about Alexylva University or its motives. Evidence appears to suggest that the organization exists in some sort of alternate universe in which Latin and Greek cultures maintain dominance at least over the Western Hemisphere; nothing to date is known about any other part of this world. All University-related objects have been found in the Mid-Southern United States, and more specifically in Tennessee, leading Foundation researchers to believe the University itself is located in that geographical area.

Many objects associated with the University (which is not believed to have built the objects) are recovered during postal transit via an agency known as "Phitransimun Combine" and accompanied by relevant paperwork, which has helped shed light on the objects and the place from which they came. To date, all that is known about the methods that transfer the objects is that the technology uses principles similar to that of the Einstein-Rosen Bridge, a concept considered purely theoretical by contemporary science. A particular section of the University known as the Department of Natural Philosophy is considered responsible for the transferences, possibly without the knowledge or consent of the rest of the organization.
groups.purpose: A university in an alternate world where Latin and Greek cultures stayed dominant. Its motives are largely unknown.
groups.gear: Objects arrive through a transfer technology that works on principles similar to an Einstein-Rosen bridge.
gearQuotes: To date, all that is known about the methods that transfer the objects is that the technology uses principles similar to that of the Einstein-Rosen Bridge, a concept considered purely theoretical by contemporary science.
groups.continuity: The brief says very little is known about the University or its motives.

groups.name: Ambrose Restaurants
lore: Overview: Ambrose Restaurants is a large-scale chain of fine-dining eateries, located in various public locations across Earth along with several locations in anomalous or extra-dimensional locations of interest. These restaurants specialize in anomalous food and culinary practices, and vary widely in variation and style. Despite the scale of the Ambrose Restaurants chain, they are generally non-hostile and will instead flee from threats directed towards them.

Ambrose Restaurants is currently believed to be jointly owned by persons of interest "Chaz Ambrose" and "Marius", but due to lack of public appearances this is unconfirmed. Notably, several groups of interest have engaged in relations with Ambrose Restaurants, including Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. and Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting, though the extent with which they collaborate is unknown. As the Ambrose Restaurants chain continues to expand beyond anomalous markets, any new locations are to be shut down and valuable information on Ambrose Restaurants saved.
groups.purpose: A chain of fine-dining restaurants serving anomalous cuisine, on Earth and in extradimensional locations.

groups.name: Anderson Robotics
lore: Overview: Based out of the Three Portlands location of interest, Anderson Robotics first came to the Foundation’s attention in 2007 with the capture of SCP-1360. Specializing in the sale of anomalous androids, robots, artificial intelligences, and cybernetics, the organization is led by a Three Portlands native and skilled thaumaturge named Vincent Anderson. Following its absorption of multiple assets from the now defunct Prometheus Labs, and its popularity within the Maxwellist Church, Anderson Robotics quickly gained a fair amount of traction in the realm of paratechnology within the 2000s and 2010s. Anderson currently uses Three Portlands as a shield, in addition to the group's remarkable espionage capabilities and overall popularity within the free port, to escape direct confrontation with the Foundation. The organization has increasingly come under scrutiny by the FBI Unusual Incidents Unit for its various attempts to influence the United States Government, with Vincent Anderson himself a particular person of interest to their Three Portlands Field Office.
groups.purpose: A Three Portlands company led by the thaumaturge Vincent Anderson. It sells anomalous androids, robots, AI and cybernetics.
groups.gear: Anomalous androids, robots, AIs and cybernetics. It also absorbed assets from the defunct Prometheus Labs.

groups.name: Arcadia
lore: Overview: Defined by highest highs and lowest lows, Arcadia was a rampage through the videogame industry driven by arcane, occult technologies that relied on luck as much as demons; but they made it work. This popularity came at the expense of their customers' exploitation and damnation - without their knowledge, of course. All that slowed to a crawl, however, after the 1983 videogame crash and the otherworld started collecting on unfulfilled promises.

Their buyout by technologic powerhouse Prism Products Corporation in 1991 revitalized the Arcadia name; albeit under shady practices and behind closed doors. The Arcadia of today is an entirely different beast - nobody is exactly sure what they do. Rumors are the only knowledge most have, but some say their longtime rival, the FBI Unusual Incidents Unit, have more that they're not spilling. If you're curious, maybe find some Arcadia to play. Because after all…
Why not Arcadia?

groups.name: Are We Cool Yet?
lore: Overview: A collective of anomalous artists, or anartists, members of Are We Cool Yet? are capable of either obtaining or producing anomalous objects and entities, which they use to create art installations. These installations are placed for maximum public exposure, and have on occasion been fatal to bystanders. The presence of the phrase "Are We Cool Yet?" is their most distinctive feature.

The collective dates back to the influence of the 19th Century paranormal renaissance on the French avant-garde art movement, particularly the "Sommes-Nous Devenus Magnifiques?" exhibition of 1874. This event has been repeated every decade since, with artists across the world striving to have their work accepted. Are We Cool Yet? lacks any centralized leadership, and while many members group together into small cells guided by an individual known as "The Critic", others prefer to have no leader, or to work alone.

Are We Cool Yet? is a well known yet controversial presence within the secretive world of anomalous art, with collectors and creators raising both moral and aesthetic objections to their work, often decrying Are We Cool Yet? as "art terrorists". The group is far from unified, and clashes of artistic vision within the movement occasionally break out in violence. These tensions have been exploited by the Foundation to apprehend anartists affiliated with Are We Cool Yet?, but preventing the general public from being exposed to their work remains challenging.
groups.purpose: A collective of anomalous artists (anartists) that builds art installations from anomalous objects and places them where the most people will see them.

groups.name: The Black Queen
lore: Overview: Little is known about the person of interest known as the Black Queen. Her identity, motives, affiliation and actions are all in doubt due to a mass of contradictory reports. It is unclear if multiple individuals utilize the title of Black Queen, or if some anomalous factor is at play to explain this discrepancy. Whatever the case, this group of interest outwardly presents under one pseudonym.

The Black Queen has been reported to operate independently, in a group of other Black Queens, or in affiliation with other groups of interest. The Black Queen has been seen cooperating with MC&D, the Chaos Insurgency and the Chicago Spectre as well as several other GOIs. Her most consistent relationship seems to be with the Serpent’s Hand, with several sources claiming that the Black Queen is a monicker of “L.S.”, rumored leader of the group. Others claim that this apparent connection is simply due to the usage of The Wanderers' Library. by both groups, and that the Black Queens use the initials ‘L.S.” to refer to “Little Sisters”, a term for novice Black Queens.

Conversely, the Black Queen has shown herself to be consistently hostile towards the Foundation. She has herself claimed to be “ Alison Chao ”, the daughter of Leanne Chao and Dr. Charles Gears, stating that her animosity stems from the belief that the Foundation forcibly enlisted her father. Due to genetic inconsistencies in retrieved biological matter, and indications of multiversal transit this claim cannot be conclusively verified. Regardless, the Black Queen seemingly believes this to be true, with many of her attacks on the Foundation relating in some capacity to Dr. Gears and his work.

Despite nominally being one individual or a small group with few resources, the Black Queen has shown herself to be very effective in disrupting Foundation operations, displaying in-depth knowledge of Foundation structures, activities and contained anomalies, repeatedly breaching Foundation security.
groups.purpose: A person or persons of interest operating under one pseudonym. Her identity, motives and affiliations are unclear.
groups.continuity: Reports are contradictory. It is unclear whether one or many individuals use the title.

groups.name: The Chaos Insurgency
lore: Overview: During the 20th century, a number of high-value assets and personnel split off from the SCP Foundation, calling themselves the " Chaos Insurgency." To this day, they remain one of the Foundation's most notorious enemies — with the overarching goal of razing the organization to the ground, and the Veil of Normalcy with it.

In pursuit of the destruction of the normalcy doctrine, no price is too great for the Insurgency. The Insurgency frequently resorts to acts of extreme violence or outright terrorism to further their goals. The organization is known for an ethos of " starting enough fires to exhaust the fire brigade," relentlessly sabotaging the Foundation to expose vulnerabilities. While most members of the Insurgency are ordinary individuals, the organization frequently makes use of anomalous items to their own benefit, especially those stolen from the Foundation.

The Insurgency overall functions as a decentralized network under which numerous cells of revolutionaries, freedom fighters, research institutes, and intelligence centers fight against the Foundation. However, at its center is the secretive "Delta Command," led by an anonymous individual known as "The Engineer." Their base of operations remains unknown.

The Insurgency's ideology is unclear, thanks in no small part to their own disinformation. Internal propaganda describes the organization as freedom fighters, uplifting the common people against the oppression of the Foundation. The Insurgency at its core seems to champion anarchist, anti-state, and radical left-wing politics, though they will frequently make use of cells from all political backgrounds.

Personnel are remain cautious of possible raids, terrorist action, and spies from the Insurgency, and are to notify their superiors about any activities from fellow personnel fitting the Insurgency behavioral profile.
groups.purpose: A splinter group of former Foundation assets and personnel whose overarching goal is to raze the Foundation and the Veil of Normalcy with it.
groups.gear: Anomalous items used to their own benefit, especially items stolen from the Foundation.
groups.continuity: The Insurgency's origins and leadership vary widely between canons and hubs.

groups.name: The Chicago Spirit
lore: Overview: During the early 20th century, the Chicago Spirit was the largest anomalous criminal organization in the Western hemisphere. Based in Chicago, Illinois, the group's influence extended to most major cities in the United States, particularly New York, Boston, New Orleans, and the extradimensional city-state of Three Portlands. The Spirit was known for recruiting individuals with anomalous capabilities, as well as creating and exploiting anomalous artifacts for use in its criminal activities.

The Spirit was founded in 1895 by Chicago resident and bar owner Richard D. Chappell, who was himself an anomalous individual. Despite years of efforts, the Foundation remained largely unsuccessful in its attempts to suppress Chappell's rise to power, due in part to its limited resources at the time as a result of an ongoing internal crisis. In January of 1919, the Foundation officially suspended all opposition against the Chicago Spirit to ensure their cooperation in preventing the spread of SCP-2680. Once allowed to operate unimpeded, the Spirit flourished into a nationwide syndicate and eventually became a driving force in the illegal distribution of alcohol during the Prohibition Era.

Thanks to the success of its bootlegging businesses, the Chicago Spirit continued to amass power over North American markets and politics throughout the 1920s, and the Foundation was eventually forced to terminate its truce with the group in order to prevent the complete dissolution of scientific normalcy. On July 11th 1933, Richard Chappell was finally apprehended by Foundation operatives following a raid on the Spirit's base of operations. In the absence of its leader, the group gradually destabilized, and most of its members and assets were acquired by other organizations. As of 1938, the Foundation officially considers the Chicago Spirit to be defunct.

However, rumors of the Spirit's continued survival have persisted in subsequent decades. Various artifacts have been discovered which imply the group's involvement, though a conclusive link has yet to be proven. Furthermore, recent evidence has revealed the emergence of a new syndicate calling itself "The Chicago Spectre", which seems to operate primarily in anomalous underground communities. Investigation into this group and its connections to the original Spirit (if any) are ongoing.
groups.purpose: The largest anomalous criminal organization in the early-20th-century Western hemisphere, based in Chicago.
groups.gear: Anomalous artifacts it created and exploited for criminal activity.
gearQuotes: The Spirit was known for recruiting individuals with anomalous capabilities, as well as creating and exploiting anomalous artifacts for use in its criminal activities.

groups.name: The Children of the Scarlet King
lore: Overview: The Children of the Scarlet King are a series of churches, organizations, individuals, and movements associated with the Pluripotent Entity known as "the Scarlet King". While the majority of Children share a set of key beliefs, the nature of their organizations, even their doctrine, varies greatly between manifestations. Discerning the Children from mundane groups of interest has thus proven difficult for the Foundation.
The true nature of the Scarlet King, or if it exists at all, is unknown.
groups.purpose: Churches, organizations, individuals and movements associated with the pluripotent entity known as the Scarlet King.
groups.continuity: Doctrine varies between manifestations, and the brief says it is unknown whether the Scarlet King exists at all.

groups.name: Church of the Broken God
lore: Overview: The Church of the Broken God is a dualistic religion that worships mechanization, regarding "flesh" as fundamentally flawed. They believe that their god has been shattered and requires reassembly, and that each of them will undergo their own apotheosis after this divine reconstruction. The church has access to multiple technological anomalies, and members of the group are frequently anomalously augmented by mechanical prosthetics, so their attempts to spread their faith more widely present an ongoing threat to Normalcy.

While similar beliefs were present in the ancient Chinese Xia Dynasty, the origins of the group are generally traced back to the Mekhanite Empire in Mycenaean Greece. Conflict with contemporaneous states, including the Daevite and Sarkic Empires, resulted in its destruction during the Bronze Age Collapse. Survivors founded the City-State of Amoni, which lasted until the 1st Century BCE. The theology of these states outlasted their demise, influencing and being influenced by Christian Gnosticism, and eventually making a resurgence during the Industrial Revolution.

The church in its modern form is divided on the question of how the reconstruction of their god is to be achieved. The largest extant denomination, the Broken Church, pursues the physical reassembly of Mekhane by bringing together anomalous artifacts, and have identified multiple SCP objects as pieces of their deity. Their leader, Robert Bumaro, has demanded that the Foundation hand over these objects to his church, and has lead multiple attempts to recover them by force. In contrast to both the Cogwork Orthodoxy and the Church of Maxwellism, members of the Broken Church traditionally refrain from any anomalous augmentation of their bodies not produced by SCP-217, and regard the doctrines of the other sects of the church as heretical.

The Cogwork Orthodoxy separated from the Broken Church during the 19th Century under the influence of wealthy industrialists, to pursue individual mechanical augmentation through a process known as "Standardization". Members of the Cogwork Orthodox Church notably reject any incorporation of modern electronics, creating complex mechanical prosthetics using both conventional and anomalous means.

The Church of Maxwellism focuses on personal augmentation through digital technology, and broke away from the rest of the Church of the Broken God in the late 20th Century, lead by a woman known as "Saint Hedwig". Maxwellists believe that by connecting together all members of the church, the collective will of humanity can "recompile" the Broken God, which they refer to as WAN. Due to their presence online and connections to Silicon Valley, Maxwellism is the most rapidly growing faction of the Church of the Broken God, despite ongoing efforts by the Foundation to limit their reach.

The Xia Anomalous Culture Group was a legendary dynasty that ruled China from 2100 to 1600 BCE. They practiced a dualistic religion that revered two entities, Father Serpent Fuxi (equivalent to the Broken God) and Mother Dragon Nüwa (equivalent to the Sarkic Yaldabaoth), and believed that the broken body of Fuxi was needed to keep Nüwa contained.

groups.name: Church of the Second Hytoth
lore: Overview: The Church of the Second Hytoth is an occult organization of human and alien entities that adhere to the extraterrestrial Ortothan religion, aiming to aid a universal guardian deity ("Rakmou-leusan") in combat against extrauniversal threats (known as "Voruteut"). The central beliefs of the religion are that the current universe, the "Second Hytoth," was preceded by a different universe, which used to exist until it was consumed by an extrauniversal entity. A group of survivors fled to the newly created Second Hytoth, our reality, with seven of them choosing to ascend to godhood to ensure the universe's safety. Six of these gods died over time, leaving Rakmou-leusan as the last survivor.

Operations taken by the Church are performed underneath the veil, likely to avoid heavy scrutiny from normalcy organizations. The main language of the group is the Ortothan Extraterrestrial Language (OEL), which has been anomalously kept unchanged despite the distances between Ortothan sects — group members attribute this to acts of divine intervention. Human Ortothan belief systems are known to have existed by ~11000 BCE, corresponding to the formation of the ancient Ortothan Kingdom civilization, though modern branches have only been developed in the past century. Ortothan groups separate from the Church exist, all being significantly smaller in comparison and tending to have differing moral beliefs.

Beyond the Church, the Ortothan religion has an interstellar and intergalactic presence, having initially emerged among extraterrestrial civilizations. Numerous such Ortothan civilizations are known to exist, with their full extent not yet ascertained. Among the largest of these is the Terzan 2 Ortothan Coalition, a collection of Ortothan entities residing in Globular Cluster Terzan 2 at war with the hostile "Twelve Stars" civilization. The only Ortothan civilization known to have entered the solar system is Species of Interest-002; it is presumed extinct.
groups.purpose: Humans and alien entities following the Ortothan religion, who aid the guardian deity Rakmou-leusan against extrauniversal threats (Voruteut).

groups.name: The Commission on Unusual Cargo
lore: Overview: One of a number of precursors to the Foundation as it exists today, the Commission on Unusual Cargo was established by the East India Company in 1623, for the purpose of containing and protecting its more peculiar cargo. It existed in this form until 1649, the year in which the group disappeared along with all of its assets, in response to a demand from the East India Company that they utilise the Unusual Cargo they had stockpiled to gain a military advantage against several large bands of privateers.

Subsequently operating in secret, the Commission continued to collect objects and entities until its merger with the Foundation in 1917. A number of these anomalous items were transferred into the Foundation's possession, along with Cargo Manifests describing the properties of and procedures for the safe storage of this cargo. This vast record of anomalous history is still being reviewed and digitised by Foundation archivists.

For as long as it was active, the Commission was headed by a merchant officer, the Right Honourable Othaniel Trower. It is unclear if this was a single, anomalously long-lived individual, or a series of multiple people using the same name. As the Commissioner of the organisation, he was overseen and advised by an eight member Board of Regents, and commanded a large staff of Wardens, Curators, and other operatives.
groups.purpose: A Foundation precursor, set up by the East India Company in 1623 to contain and protect peculiar cargo. It vanished in 1649 rather than weaponize that cargo.
groups.gear: Its stockpiled anomalous cargo. Some items, with their Cargo Manifests, later passed to the Foundation.

groups.name: The Daevites
lore: The information contained within this file cannot be authenticated with 100% certainty, due to the anomalous nature of content. As with all atemporal retrocausal anomalies, a healthy skepticism is recommended when discussing or researching the information on the Daevas. If, in reviewing this file, you notice inaccuracies or discrepancies with baseline reality, please report to your on-Site RAISA representative. —Maria Jones, RAISA Director

Overview: The Daevite Empire was an ancient civilization originating in what is now south-central Siberia. The Empire represented a stratified society structured around systemic slavery, military conquest through various anomalous means, ancestor worship, ritualized human sacrifice, and the widespread usage of thaumaturgical practices.

The history of the Daevite Empire is nebulous and awash with mystery due to the influence of SCP-140: a book entitled “A Chronicle of the Daevas” which has the anomalous effect of retroactive temporal causality. If SCP-140 comes into contact with any fluid suitable for writing, including human blood, its account of the Daevite civilization's history expands - often pushing its final collapse closer to the present - and baseline reality retroactively changes to reflect this new history. Projections suggest a high-casualty CK-class restructuring scenario should the Empire reemerge in the modern day through retrocasual means.

Historical accounts and archaeological findings suggest that the Empire began as a loosely connected series of Neolithic city-states later united by a strongly-matriarchal aristocracy (the "Daeva") with potential anomalous enhancements. Religious practices were then centered around the veneration of life (the "Font"), with blood being the medium by which life travels. Other accounts detail extensive conflict with the ancient Chinese, Mongol, and Ortothan states and other neighboring civilizations, as well as slave revolts spearheaded by the precursor to the modern Sarkic Cults. However, it is important to understand that by the very nature of SCP-140, the history of the Daevites has changed numerous times: what specifics can be read about the development of their Empire must be taken with scholarly skepticism by virtue of their atemporal nature.
groups.purpose: An ancient, stratified civilization built on slavery, conquest, ancestor worship, human sacrifice and thaumaturgy.
groups.gear: Thaumaturgical practices and "various anomalous means" of conquest.
gearQuotes: The Empire represented a stratified society structured around systemic slavery, military conquest through various anomalous means, ancestor worship, ritualized human sacrifice, and the widespread usage of thaumaturgical practices.
groups.continuity: The brief warns that its information cannot be authenticated with certainty, because the Daevites are an atemporal, retrocausal anomaly.

groups.name: Dark Sushi
lore: Japanese Group of Interest Name: 闇寿司 (Yamisushi)

Overview: Dark Sushi is a group of sushi chefs who deal primarily with food-related anomalies. The organizational structure is similar to a chain or goodwill in the restaurant industry, and consists of multiple restaurants and employees per restaurant.

Several members have similar anomalies to SCP-1134-JP. However, the "sushi" used by Dark Sushi includes foods not generally classified as sushi, and the anomalous effects (designated SCP-1134-JP-1) produced by such foods are unpredictable. Moreover, the group is actively recruiting new members and developing technology related to SCP-1134-JP-1.

The origins of Dark Sushi, such as the date of its founding and founder, are unclear, but the current leader has been identified as the person known as Yami (闇), meaning "the Dark". While details of its organization policy are unknown, research suggests that the group is motivated in part by dissatisfaction with traditional sushi-eating culture.

In recent years, Dark Sushi has rapidly grown within in the paranormal food community, which may have been accomplished through psychological manipulation techniques utilized by the group, and most members have no qualms about using violence and heavy-handed coercion. The Foundation remains vigilant for Dark Sushi as it continues to expand and establish links with other Groups of Interest.
groups.purpose: A restaurant-style network of sushi chefs dealing in food-related anomalies. Translated from the Japanese branch (闇寿司).
groups.gear: Develops technology related to SCP-1134-JP-1.
gearQuotes: Moreover, the group is actively recruiting new members and developing technology related to SCP-1134-JP-1.

groups.name: Deer College
lore: Overview: Deer College is a coeducational liberal arts and occult sciences college in the heart of scenic Three Portlands, an extra-dimensional city-state located adjacent to the American Northweast and Southern England; with a curriculum that focuses on the marriage of mundane and occult disciplines and a well-regarded Anart program, Deer is often seen as the liberal arts counterpart to its Global Occult Coalition sponsored rival across town, ICSUT Portlands. A number of prominent figures in the anomalous world are Deer alumni, including Vincent Anderson, the CEO of Anderson Robotics, and Esther "lesbian_gengar" Kogan, one of the co-founders of Gamers Against Weed.

As the Foundation's operations in Three Portlands are heavily restricted by a number of agreements with the FBI's Unusual Incidents Unit, Deer College itself is relatively free of Foundation intervention; however, all Deer alumni are automatically marked as persons of interest, and may be subject to increased Foundation scrutiny.
groups.purpose: A liberal arts and occult sciences college in Three Portlands, often seen as the counterpart to the GOC-sponsored ICSUT Portlands.

groups.name: Doctor Wondertainment
lore: Overview Dr. Wondertainment is an individual or group capable of producing anomalous artifacts and entities. Most of these resemble toys for children to play with, but Dr. Wondertainment branding has also been found other products, including video games and breakfast cereal. Dr Wondertainment also produced the “Little Misters”, a series of anomalous humanoids that appear to be intended as collectibles.

Little concrete information is available about Dr. Wondertainment as either a person or an organization, and estimates of its size range from it being a single person with anomalous abilities to a large corporation with hundreds of employees and dozens of departments. Multiple individuals have been identified as "Doctor Wondertainment", but it is unclear whether this is the group's founder, their current successor, or simply a brand mascot.

Although the Foundation actively obstructs Dr. Wondertainment's commercial activities by containing their merchandise, they appear to regard this as both a cost of doing business and as an opportunity for free product testing, and have even expressed appreciation for the Foundation’s efforts. Despite this lack of overt hostility, they remain a threat to normalcy due to their continued production and distribution of anomalies.

Marshall, Carter and Dark has been involved in the sale of Dr. Wondertainment products, and commercial ties between the two groups are being investigated. A link between Dr. Wondertainment and the Factory is suspected, since both are capable of mass-producing anomalies, but has not been confirmed.
groups.purpose: An individual or group that produces anomalous artifacts and entities, most of them resembling children's toys.
groups.gear: Its anomalous products are its output. The brief documents no weapons or equipment.
gearQuotes: Wondertainment is an individual or group capable of producing anomalous artifacts and entities.

groups.name: The Factory
lore: Overview: The Factory is a brand name associated with a wide variety of anomalous objects, all of which appear to have been mass-produced using specialized equipment. Little is known about the actual group responsible for these products, their means of production, or their motives for selling them to consumers.

The Factory appears to either operate in partnership with existing manufacturing plants, or by reopening and repurposing previously abandoned facilities. The workers in these buildings are frequently injured by the equipment they use, but are coerced into continuing work for little or no pay, often relying on crude mechanical prostheses. It is believed that one or more anomalous entities are responsible for the recruitment and management of the Factory's human personnel. Recovered documents occasionally reference an individual known as “The Investor", but little is known about this figure.

The Factory has had a number of commercial relationships with other Groups of Interest, including Marshall, Carter, & Dark and The Chicago Spirit. The paranormal community regards the Factory with suspicion or outright hostility, both due to the dangers posed by their products and their notorious mistreatment of their employees. Many paratechnology companies still make use of anomalous materials and components produced by the Factory, primarily due to a lack of affordable alternatives.
Past connections between the Foundation and The Factory are currently under internal investigation.
groups.purpose: A brand behind a wide range of mass-produced anomalous objects. Little is known about who runs it or why.

groups.name: Febris Pharmaceuticals
lore: Italian Group of Interest Name: Febris Farmaceutica

Overview: Febris Pharmaceuticals is a company founded by the Farnesi family in the 1960s, specializing in the research and sale of medicines for both sides of the Veil, using thaumaturgical knowledge passed down from the Roman goddess Febris, Goddess of Malarial Fever and Healing.

The origins of this Group of Interest can be traced back to the Cult of Febris, a group of serial poisoners in Imperial Rome. Led by Lucusta in the 1st century AD, their sect was violently repressed by Emperor Galba in 69 AD, and their tablets, which contained the goddess's knowledge for the creation of toxins and diseases, were believed lost. Unbeknownst to Galba and his men, the tablets had been magically hidden, remaining secret until the will of the Goddess would lead the right person to find them.

Anticipating the arrival of scientific discoveries that could increase their power, in 1960 Febris created an heir, mixing her divine essence with the blood of Filippo Farnesi, an archaeologist who discovered one of her last places of worship. Having unwillingly become a pawn in the goddess's plan, Filippo founded Febris Pharmaceuticals while waiting for his son, the young Fausto, to take over. Becoming CEO in 1989, Fausto Farnesi recovered the tablets and, after deciphering their contents, began the creation of a clinical thaumaturgy that combined ancient knowledge with new biochemical and biotechnological technologies, opening a new frontier in the development of drugs and toxins that had characterized the ancient Cult of Febris.

Given the Foundation's growing interest in their activities, in the following years Febris Pharmaceuticals consolidated its dominance in Free Port of Gorična, the largest Free Port in Southern Europe, obtaining a potentially protected headquarters from Foundation investigations from which to continue its expansion into the international (and interdimensional) market.
groups.purpose: A company founded by the Farnesi family that sells medicines on both sides of the Veil. Translated from the Italian branch.
groups.gear: Clinical thaumaturgy that combines ancient knowledge with biochemical and biotechnological methods.
gearQuotes:
Italian Group of Interest Name: Febris Farmaceutica

Overview: Febris Pharmaceuticals is a company founded by the Farnesi family in the 1960s, specializing in the research and sale of medicines for both sides of the Veil, using thaumaturgical knowledge passed down from the Roman goddess Febris, Goddess of Malarial Fever and Healing.

Becoming CEO in 1989, Fausto Farnesi recovered the tablets and, after deciphering their contents, began the creation of a clinical thaumaturgy that combined ancient knowledge with new biochemical and biotechnological technologies, opening a new frontier in the development of drugs and toxins that had characterized the ancient Cult of Febris.

groups.name: Fifthism
lore: "This church is to other churches what clowns are to people. There are some superficial similarities, but all the wrong things are being emphasized and exaggerated so you can't quite put your finger on what is wrong… Sure, it isn't out to get you, but what does it mean? Why is it there? What happens if it calls to you?" — Researcher Emile Metcalfe

Overview: The Fifth Church came to the Foundation's attention in 2005 following the publication of "Star Signals", a cognitohazardous self-help book intended to spread their ideology to the general public. The Foundation maintains a watchlist of individuals confirmed or suspected to be associated with the Church, which includes many celebrities and prominent personalities in the entertainment industry, although Operation Stargazer protocol dictates that the names of these individuals are to be censored. While the Fifth Church has never communicated directly with the SCP Foundation, it is considered to be a hostile force.

Other manifestations of Fifthism have since been documented, loosely connected or entirely unrelated to the Fifth Church. These include the First Southern Fifth Church, the musical group Constellation Starfish, and the private spaceflight start-up Quintessence Aerospace, with similar cults dating back to antiquity. While these groups vary greatly in form and doctrine, they share many traits, most notably a fixation on stars, starfish, and the number five.
groups.purpose: The Fifth Church, a religious movement that came to Foundation attention in 2005 and is centred on the concept of "the Fifth".

groups.name: Gamers Against Weed
lore: Overview: "Gamers Against Weed" is a loosely-organized confederation of anomalous individuals, as well as associates thereof, that produce or procure anomalies for satirical purposes and/or for their own amusement. More recently, however, they have also been implicated in supplying anomalies to left-wing political organizations. While Gamers Against Weed organizes its activities primarily over internet channels, several real-world locations associated with the group have been identified and raided. Current intelligence suggests that Gamers Against Weed is in the process of creating and distributing a set of anomalous humanoids to parody Dr. Wondertainment's "Little Misters" series, and that it is aware of the Foundation's operations, if not its exact nature.

Detainment of Gamers Against Weed's members has proven more difficult than anticipated. Some of the group's organizers are believed to possess reality-altering capabilities, either in their own right or through access to outside resources. Current operations are focused on the containment of related anomalies and the identification and analysis of Gamers Against Weed's most dangerous members.
groups.purpose: A loose online confederation of anomalous individuals who make or procure anomalies for satire or amusement.

groups.name: Global Occult Coalition (GOC)
lore: Overview: The Global Occult Coalition (GOC) was founded after the conclusion of the Seventh Occult War, a covert conflict taking place during World War II. The victorious Allied Occult Initiative recruited defectors from the defeated Axis powers to establish a new organisation, tasked with protecting humanity and concealing the existence of the anomalous. The GOC regard themselves as the police of the paranormal world, responsible for the elimination of any "parathreat" they identify.

Although the GOC is a political force affiliated with the United Nations, they are lead by the Council of 108, consisting of the most influential organizations in the paranormal community. This diverse group of occultists, psychics, priests and scientists includes the Bavarian Illuminati, the Knights Templar, the Servants of the Silicon Nornir, the International Center for the Study of Unified Thaumatology (ICSUT), the World Parahealth Organization, and Goldbaker-Reinz Ltd. These groups supply the GOC with advanced experimental technology, as well as expertise in Applied Thaumatology, which are both utilized by the GOC's PHYSICS Division to detect and destroy anomalies.

The GOC and the Foundation share many of the same goals and adversaries, which has enabled the coordination of joint operations in the past. However, while the GOC has enough respect for the might of the Foundation to avoid open conflict, they object to the Foundation's practice of containing SCP objects, and GOC operatives in the field will strive to neutralize anomalies before the Foundation can recover them. Although overt confrontation of this group must be avoided, GOC agents are to be treated with suspicion at all times.

The International Center for the Study of Unified Thaumatology (ICSUT) has campuses around the world, either concealed within conventional institutions of higher education or operating openly in paranormal Freeports such as Three Portlands. ICSUT staff research the anomalous phenomena known as thaumaturgy, and educate students in both the theory underlying Unified Thaumatology and the practice of Applied Thaumatology. The majority of the GOC's mages are ICSUT alumni.

The Servants of the Silicon Nornir are a transhumanist religion, and worship and maintain three supercomputers named after the three Norns of Norse Mythology. They are responsible for the founding of the extradimensional city of EURTEC, a paranormal enclave in which most of the GOC's advanced and anomalous technology is researched and developed.

The World Parahealth Organization (WPHO) is a division of the World Health Organization dedicated to the study and treatment of paranormal diseases, including hemovorism and transformative lycanthropy. They generally agree with the Foundation that vectors of these diseases need to be contained, but advocate for their release once no longer infectious.
groups.purpose: Founded after the Seventh Occult War to protect humanity and conceal the anomalous. It sees itself as the police of the paranormal world.
specialties: UN-affiliated, led by the Council of 108
groups.gear: Advanced experimental technology and Applied Thaumatology from Council members, used by the PHYSICS Division to detect and destroy anomalies.

groups.name: Goldbaker-Reinz Ltd.
lore: Overview: Goldbaker-Reinz Ltd. is one of the foremost insurance providers for the anomalous world. It provides insurance to both individuals and institutions, as well as reinsurance, data vending, risk analysis, and forensic & enforcement services. It is known throughout the anomalous world for always honoring the letter of its contracts in good faith. It holds a seat on the Global Occult Coalition's Council of 108 due to the trust its predecessors gained from substantial recovery services provided in the wake of the Seventh Occult War, and it continues to provide services to the GOC, the Foundation, and many more.

The modern incarnation of Goldbaker-Reinz merged from Goldbaker Ltd., led by the enigmatic Goldbaker, and the Reinz Group led by Werner Reinz in 1981 after other founding members of the Reinz Group vanished in mysterious circumstances. The origin and full history of Goldbaker are lost to time, though individuals with similar titles or names have been providing similar services stretching back to the dawn of human civilization — and possibly beyond.

The Foundation has a number of outstanding contracts with Goldbaker-Reinz. Policies range from the mundane, such as standard personnel insurance health and life insurance, to the largely financial, such as providing beryllium bronze and other materials at fixed prices in the event of containment failure, to the rare and exotic, such as procurement of oxygenating algae in the event of a GH-Class Dead Greenhouse scenario. A number of these policies are redundant with the Foundation's own contingencies, but for two such risk averse groups such redundancy proves reassuring.

These contracts were entered into in good faith, but the Foundation also views them as a means of maintaining an accurate and up-to-date understanding of the inner workings of Goldbaker-Reinz. The Foundation is cognizant of Goldbaker-Reinz's position of power within the anomalous world, so the goal of contract negotiations is to minimize the money and information given while maximizing the coverage and information received. Despite this perennial game of cat-and-mouse, the Foundation and Goldbaker-Reinz still consider each other trustworthy — at least enough to conduct business.
groups.purpose: One of the foremost insurers of the anomalous world, offering insurance, reinsurance, data vending, risk analysis and enforcement.
specialties: Seat on the GOC Council of 108

groups.name: Greazeburger Incorporated
lore: Overview: I know you're watching. You're looking for something to read, aren't you? I wish I could read. I can't do anything else either. I'm stuck here, warped into… just a few sorry little bundles of information designed to advertise the people who made me this way.

Greazeburger Incorporated, that merry bunch. I used to be a salesman for them, ya know. Before I fucked up and got turned into whatever this paragraph is. It was the happiest time of my life and I just didn't know it. I even had the classic getup, dress shirt with striped suspenders, a straw boater - even shoes shined so much I could see my toothy grin in them if the sun hit them right.

I don't have any of that now, not since I flushed my dream sale down the toilet. All I have is this space on the page, right here, and just a few sentences of space to lure in new customers to the Greazeburger Literary Universe. And that's that!
Have fun reading! - Jimmy Greaze, Salesman Extraordinaire
groups.purpose: An anomalous fast-food corporation. Its directory brief is written in-universe by a former salesman who was turned into the text itself.

groups.name: GRU Division "P"
lore: Russian Group of Interest Name: ГРУ, Отдел 'П'

Overview: A division of the Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) of both the Soviet Union and the Russian Federation, the "P" is an abbreviation of Psychotronics, a term for psychic abilities widely used in Soviet paranormal research. Throughout its existence, Division "P" focused on the acquisition and creation of anomalies useful for furthering the economic and political objectives of the Soviet Union. The GRU-P was also tasked with anomalous surveillance of the Soviet Union's adversaries, as well as the suppression of paranormal criminal and religious groups.

The department was originally established in early 1935 as the ЧД АКН ("ChD AKN", or Fourth Department Abnormal Occurrences Commission), tasked by direct decree of Josef Stalin with investigating the murder of Sergei Kirov. During the Second World War, the Commission was expanded into a division of the newly reorganized GRU, and focused on developing paranormal weaponry and countering anomalous threats from Nazi Germany. During the Cold War, the organization shifted its focus to the USA and its allies, escalating tensions with capitalist countries by developing anomalous weapons of mass destruction. The Soviet Union did not regard the Foundation as a neutral party in this conflict, and the GRU-P seized control of Foundation facilities and anomalies, constraining Foundation operations in the Soviet Bloc.

After 1991, rapid restructuring and budget cuts resulted in GRU Division "P" losing numerous anomalies and personnel. While many were acquired by the Foundation, the European black market was flooded with anomalous items formerly held by the GRU-P, and numerous personnel were recruited into the private sector (particularly by Marshal, Carter and Dark) or by the Chaos Insurgency. GRU Division "P" continues to exist as a paranormal agency within the Russian Federation, but with a drastically reduced budget its remaining personnel no longer obstruct Foundation's operations within Russia.
groups.purpose: The psychotronics division of Soviet and Russian military intelligence. It acquires and creates anomalies for state objectives.
groups.gear: Paranormal weaponry against Nazi Germany, then anomalous weapons of mass destruction in the Cold War.
gearQuotes: During the Second World War, the Commission was expanded into a division of the newly reorganized GRU, and focused on developing paranormal weaponry and countering anomalous threats from Nazi Germany.
During the Cold War, the organization shifted its focus to the USA and its allies, escalating tensions with capitalist countries by developing anomalous weapons of mass destruction.

groups.name: His/Her Majesty's Foundation for the Secure Containment of the Paranormal (HMFSCP)
lore: Overview: Prior to the Convention on Preternatural Phenomena, several prenormalcy agencies oversaw the study and/or the containment of the anomalous. One such organisation was His/Her Majesty's Foundation for the Secure Containment of the Paranormal, also known as His/Her Majesty's Foundation for the Study of Curiosities and Phantasmagoria. One of the oldest paranatural organisations in history, His/Her Majesty's Foundation oversaw all paranatural phenomenon and threats across the British Isles and beyond, paving the way for many methodologies in anomalous research and containment.

In operation since the fifth century C.E., the group have been a secret pillar in British history, overseeing its several invasions, blossoming trade routes, industrial revolutions and its eventual height as the British Empire. However, following the Sixth Occult War, the group officially dissolved and joined with 12 other organisations to form the current Foundation. Though now seen as a relic of the past, their prior works have continued to be both hindrance and help to the modern Foundation. Even today, many of the anomalous objects and entities contained in the UK were inherited from this group.
groups.purpose: One of the oldest paranatural organizations: a pre-Foundation British crown agency for studying and containing the anomalous.

groups.name: Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting
lore: Overview: Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting is purported to be a circus of anomalous origin and purpose. Currently, there is no evidence that this group exists beyond the allegations of various sapient SCPs and a handful of damaged non-anomalous artifacts. Most related objects typified by humanoid status utilize anomalous deformities for the sake of performance in some way, such as SCP-1884 and SCP-2902. Others appear to be typical fairground objets d'art, such as SCP-1921, or take the form of 'attractions' for the show, such as SCP-3717 or SCP-1695. Typically, objects related to Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting are found at fairgrounds where the show is said to have 'performed.'
groups.purpose: A purported circus of anomalous origin. Its members perform using anomalous deformities.
gearQuotes: Currently, there is no evidence that this group exists beyond the allegations of various sapient SCPs and a handful of damaged non-anomalous artifacts.
groups.continuity: The brief notes there is no evidence it exists beyond allegations by sapient SCPs and a few artifacts.

groups.name: The Horizon Initiative
lore: Overview: The Horizon Initiative is an organization created in the late 1960s by various influential sects in the main three Abrahamic religions as a response to the growing number of anomalous activities and groups which they perceived as threats. Though the full extent of their goals is uncertain, the Horizon Initiative is known to target SCP objects, either with the intention of retrieving or destroying them, depending on each item's perceived place in their dogma.

The Initiative is led by a tribunal composed of leaders from the three largest sects involved in its creation, though a large amount of internal strife often leaves the official leadership in less than full control of the organization. The HI's main combat force, Project Malleus, is generally deployed in anti-cult operations and in SCP retrieval operations.

The Initiative's relations with most other Groups of Interest and the Foundation seems to be in a state of constant flux; while all parts of the HI perceive the Church of the Broken God and Fifth Church with a great degree of hostility (and at times engaging them in armed conflict), sentiments toward the Foundation and the GOC vary greatly, from open hostility to a limited willingness to cooperate, depending on the internal affiliation of individual members.
groups.purpose: Created in the late 1960s by sects of the three main Abrahamic religions, in response to anomalies and groups they saw as threats.
groups.gear: Targets SCP objects for retrieval or destruction, depending on each item's place in its dogma.
gearQuotes: The Initiative's relations with most other Groups of Interest and the Foundation seems to be in a state of constant flux; while all parts of the HI perceive the Church of the Broken God and Fifth Church with a great degree of hostility (and at times engaging them in armed conflict), sentiments toward the Foundation and the GOC vary greatly, from open hostility to a limited willingness to cooperate, depending on the internal affiliation of individual members.

groups.name: Imperial Japanese Anomalous Matters Examination Agency (IJAMEA)
lore: Japanese Group of Interest Name: 大日本帝国異常事例調査局

Overview: The Imperial Japanese Anomalous Matters Examination Agency (IJAMEA) was Japan's official and primary agency responsible for anomalies in the period from the Meiji Restoration in 1868 until the end of World War II in 1945. IJAMEA was founded to bring Japan up to speed with Western esoteric research, acting as a modern counterpart to pre-existing groups regarded as "primitive". In this capacity, the IJAMEA catalogued hundreds of different anomalies spread throughout Japan and her colonies, conducted extensive research on these, and undertook numerous projects aiming to utilize the anomalous for the greater good of the fledgling Empire.

IJAMEA saw its most significant role during WWII, when it attempted to weaponize several anomalies to assist military forces in the war against the Allies. However, rushed planning and insufficient funds resulted in few of these programmes bearing fruit. IJAMEA was formally disbanded with the Treaty of San Francisco in 1951, and most of its assets were either transferred to GOC control or covertly acquired by the Foundation.

However, imperial loyalists and Japanese nationalists within it kept IJAMEA alive in the post-War years, this time as a clandestine organization, during which its main focus was checking the spread of communist influence in Japan and East Asia. Today, it primarily serves to care for the well-being of Japan's diverse but faltering anomalous ecology, and supports various nationalist agendas with its ties to prominent politicians, businesspeople and cultural personalities throughout Japan. It seeks to return some political power to the Imperial family and return Japan to great power status, and actively seeks to exploit the various anomalies in its possession for this purpose. The Foundation is seen as a foreign rival at best, and agents are to exercise due caution when interacting with IJAMEA personnel.
groups.purpose: Japan's official anomalies agency from the Meiji Restoration (1868) until 1945. Translated from the Japanese branch.
groups.gear: Attempted to weaponize several anomalies to support Japanese forces in WWII.
gearQuotes: IJAMEA saw its most significant role during WWII, when it attempted to weaponize several anomalies to assist military forces in the war against the Allies.

groups.name: Just Girly Things
lore: Overview: Just Girly Things is an anomalous internet blog focused on encouraging girls to partake in traditionally feminine aesthetics and activities. The website went online in 2010, after beginning as a magazine in 2006, and is inaccessible to any individual with a Y chromosome.

The Just Girly Things website, and other products associated with the group, exhibit a memetic effect, compelling subjects with an XX karyotype to join the group and adhere to its leader's conception of traditional gender roles for women, even when those directly conflict with the subject's prior political beliefs or gender identity. Members of Just Girly Things tend to exhibit manipulative behavior towards those around them, doing anything they can to spread the group's ideals more broadly. GOI-4319 is considered particularly dangerous due to its highly infectious nature.

The founder of GOI-4319 is POI-4319, a charismatic reality bender known as “KeeLee”. POI-4319 has demonstrated a powerful ability to compel others to adopt its way of thinking, through a combination of social manipulation and anomalous means.
groups.purpose: An anomalous blog that pushes traditionally feminine activities through a memetic effect, and is inaccessible to anyone with a Y chromosome.

groups.name: The Mages Academy
lore: German Group of Interest Name: Die Magierakademie

Overview: The Mages Academy is a group with locations in several European countries, headquartered in Germany, whose mission is to explore and teach the safe use of anomalous skills in the form of "magic". While the Foundation considers anomalies to be a danger and tries to control them by all means, the Academy sees anomalies as a natural part of the world and tries to achieve a harmonious coexistence, by dealing with anomalies in a largely non-violent and scientific way.

The Academy has covert agents in most of the major locations of the German-speaking Foundation, and some in Europe, who observe the Foundation's work, exert influence here and there, and coordinate secret support or countermeasures through the Academy. Since its exposure by Acolytes of the Fourth Reich, the Academy has kept a low profile, but has recently taken the initiative and is now trying to work with the Foundation.
groups.purpose: A European academy (headquartered in Germany) that explores and teaches the safe use of anomalous abilities as "magic". Translated from the German branch.
specialties: Anomalies as a natural part of the world

groups.name: Manna Charitable Foundation
lore: Overview: Established in 1971 as an interfaith humanitarian relief agency, recovered documents describe the Manna Charitable Foundation's mission as "sharing all of God's miracles with the least of His children". Funded indirectly through associations with various charitable groups and religious organizations, and on occasion publicly endorsed by wealthy philanthropists or academic institutions, the MCF's primary agenda since its founding has been the free distribution of anomalous objects, or their by-products, to civilians living in poverty-stricken regions in the Third World or in areas afflicted by warfare, famine, or natural disaster.

The MCF is currently recognized as a non-governmental organization by the United Nations, and is known to operate legally and illegally in several hostile or isolated regions outside the Foundation's sphere of influence. While no SCP objects known to have been distributed by the MCF to date have caused intentional harm to human beings or communities (and detained MCF operatives tend to demonstrate strong pacifist beliefs), containment breaches associated with the group have often resulted in human casualties or severe threats to the global status quo due to unforeseen consequences of the object's release from containment, and/or a zeal to distribute potentially "helpful" objects immediately without rigorous scientific study of their long-term behavior.
groups.purpose: An interfaith humanitarian relief agency founded in 1971 to share "God's miracles", meaning anomalies, with those in need.

groups.name: Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd.
lore: Overview: An anomalous goods and services broker primarily based in London, England, with satellite offices in Hong Kong and New York. Catering to the super-rich, with extensive political and financial ties worldwide (particularly within sub-Veil communities), this group has caused extensive problems for the Foundation. Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. is known for collecting rare and obscure items, along with providing its clients the most exclusive, expensive, and rare experiences available, no matter the cost to human life.

These activities have resulted in conflict with the Foundation on numerous occasions. The group is not known for the use of force; they prefer to apply extreme financial and political pressure to achieve their goals. When forced to use more direct means, Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. employs outside agents, often nameless contractors embedded within hundreds of layers of shell companies. This makes it difficult to understand the true of their activities in the mundane and paranormal worlds, particularly where their executives are involved.

Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. has caused several SCP containment breaches, primarily through the use of money or social pressure. Many reports, records, and even anomalies have been leaked by Foundation personnel, influenced by the promise of large amounts of money or the threat of blackmail.

Information pertaining to Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd., such as the name of the director or even a list of members, has proven very difficult to acquire. Agents encountering members of this group are advised to maintain a cover story and not reveal, for any reason, their Foundation ties or any SCP information. Double-agents are advised not to get comfortable with the life Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. affords those affiliated with them, as these privileges can and will be taken away if they are discovered.
groups.purpose: A London-based broker of anomalous goods and services for the super-rich, with offices in Hong Kong and New York.
groups.gear: Rare and obscure anomalous items it collects and offers to clients.

groups.name: Medician Academy of Occult Art
lore: Italian Group of Interest Name: Medicea Accademia dell’Arte Occulta (MADAO)

Overview: One of the most ancient and renowned academic institutions in the anomalous world, the Medician Academy of Occult Art is based in Florence, Italy. It was founded in the late 15th century by Lorenzo de’ Medici, lord of Florence and patron of arts, and during the Renaissance the Academy was able to spread its influence across most nations of Europe and the courts of the Old Continent. The activities promoted by the Academy included teaching art techniques and the collection of old anomalous artifacts from ancient cultures.

From the mid 18th century, after going through a brief period of decadence, the Academy was able to recover and create new branches in new countries across new continents. The institution oriented its activity towards the recovery and restoration of art pieces, developing a its own particular aesthetic taste. This led to hostile relations with the AWCY? movement, which is considered the main rival of the Academy.
groups.purpose: An ancient Florentine academy of occult art, founded in the late 15th century by Lorenzo de' Medici. Translated from the Italian branch.
groups.gear: Old anomalous artifacts collected from ancient cultures.
gearQuotes: The activities promoted by the Academy included teaching art techniques and the collection of old anomalous artifacts from ancient cultures.

groups.name: "Nobody"
lore: Overview: Little is currently known about the person, entity, or group known as "Nobody". First sighted in 1954, they have had numerous appearances since. There has only been one person seen at any given time, typically described as a male Caucasian dressed in a grey suit and a fedora. If asked his identity, he replies that he's "Nobody". However, it is not known if this is the work of a single person or multiple agents of a single, unknown agency. Their agenda is currently unknown, sometimes helping the Foundation, sometimes hindering it. Caution is recommended if any field agents encounter an operative identifying themselves as "Nobody".
groups.purpose: A person, entity or group known only as "Nobody", first sighted in 1954.
groups.continuity: It is not known whether "Nobody" is one person or several agents.

groups.name: Office For The Reclamation of Islamic Artifacts (ORIA)
lore: Overview: The Office For The Reclamation of Islamic Artifacts (ORIA) is a paramilitary force dedicated to the collection, documentation and utilization of anomalous phenomena throughout the Middle East and Central Asia. Despite its name, the group does not limit itself to the pursuit of objects of Islamic origin.

Although the group existed prior to the 1979 overthrow of the Imperial Iranian government, they rose to prominence through collaboration with the nascent Islamic Republic of Iran, and were instrumental in the expulsion of Foundation personnel from Iran as "agents of colonialism." Iranian forces occupied Foundation Sites, and attempts at maintaining a clandestine presence in the region were met with failure, resulting in the majority of Foundation personnel in Iran being either captured or killed.

Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini formally made ORIA part of the new government by secret decree in 1981, assigning them significant funds to prevent Iran from falling behind in the field of extranormal research. While ORIA has access to considerable resources, including arrangements with reality-warping djinn, its effectiveness is hobbled by infighting among numerous factions within the organization. Some of these disputes center around philosophical and theological differences, while others appear to be personal in nature. It is theorized that ORIA has multiple commanders with overlapping responsibilities to prevent any one individual from accumulating too much power within the organization, as this could to pose a challenge to the Supreme Leader.

With the spread of Iranian hegemony throughout the Middle East and Western Asia, ORIA has expanded its reach across the region, becoming the foremost paranormal organization in the Islamic world. Although cooperation agreements have been negotiated in the past, ORIA should still be considered a hostile force, and Foundation personnel are advised to use extreme caution when engaging.
groups.purpose: A paramilitary force that collects, documents and uses anomalies across the Middle East and Central Asia.
groups.gear: Anomalous phenomena collected for use. The brief notes it is not limited to objects of Islamic origin.
gearQuotes: Overview: The Office For The Reclamation of Islamic Artifacts (ORIA) is a paramilitary force dedicated to the collection, documentation and utilization of anomalous phenomena throughout the Middle East and Central Asia.

groups.name: Oneiroi Collective
lore: Overview: Information about the Oneiroi Collective has come to the Foundation only through analysis and interviews or the anomalous objects they leave behind. It is believed to be a collective consciousness of dreaming persons and dream-based entities.

Intelligence has shown that they have been documented by other Groups of Interest, usually to a degree similar to the Foundation's interaction. The Oneiroi Collective is apparently capable of contacting even highly isolated entities (e.g. "Nobody"). Their goals, if any exist, are currently unknown.
groups.purpose: Believed to be a collective consciousness of dreaming people and dream-based entities.
groups.continuity: Known only from anomalous objects it leaves behind and from interviews.

groups.name: Parawatch
lore: Overview: The Parawatch Wiki is an online web forum of conspiracy theorists, paranormal enthusiasts, and amateur writers, operating with the intent of investigating and exposing anomalous phenomena. The group primarily compiles short stories on their forum, detailing encounters with paranormal phenomena, historical cases, and any unusual events users have experienced. Further operation and any potential impact on normalcy is hindered by the geographic spread of the userbase and the lack of central coordination.

Despite investment in the paranormal, Parawatch has no knowledge on the nature of anomalous phenomena, the Veil, and the Foundation's existence. This in tandem with public obscurity has prevented them from potentially endangering the Veil. The group is currently being left active as a means of misinforming and misleading other investigations into the anomalous.
groups.purpose: An online forum of conspiracy theorists and paranormal enthusiasts who investigate and try to expose anomalous phenomena.

groups.name: Prometheus Labs, Inc.
lore: Overview: Founded in 1892, Prometheus Labs was dedicated to researching anomalous objects for use in developing new technologies. Over the years, Prometheus Labs developed into a multinational conglomerate selling advanced and anomalous technologies to governments, militaries, and Groups of Interest. Throughout its history, Prometheus Labs displayed a nominal amount of cooperation with Foundation efforts to protect normalcy, and at times even collaborated with the Foundation, but refused to cease its study of anomalies and resisted Foundation oversight.

In 1998, following a long period of financial decline, the Prometheus Labs conglomerate was dissolved, resulting in the creation of numerous successor companies formed from its subsidiaries. The breakup of the conglomerate was fraught with technical and administrative difficulties, resulting in the loss of many products and the layoffs of numerous personnel. Most of the former projects of Prometheus Labs now in containment were recovered during this time, and many of its former employees were hired by the Foundation.
groups.purpose: Founded in 1892 to research anomalies for new technologies, it became a conglomerate selling them to governments and militaries.
groups.gear: Advanced and anomalous technologies sold to governments, militaries and Groups of Interest.
gearQuotes: Overview: Founded in 1892, Prometheus Labs was dedicated to researching anomalous objects for use in developing new technologies.
Over the years, Prometheus Labs developed into a multinational conglomerate selling advanced and anomalous technologies to governments, militaries, and Groups of Interest.

groups.name: Pseudogenesis Productions
lore: Overview: Pseudogenesis Productions is a small, anomalous theater company, focused on creating immersive and innovative theatrical productions through the use of memetic and ontological anomalies. With a central team of four, Pseudogenesis collaborates with local anartists and performers to make one-of-a-kind experiences, to give everybody a chance to see the world from a new perspective.

Despite the relatively benign anomalies and performances they create, The Foundation does whatever they can to stop them; their refusal to respect the Veil has led to many conflicts, and circumstances where the only option The Foundation has left is convincing the audience that "it's all part of the show".
Tickets sell out fast, so don't wait — come see a performance today! RAISA NOTE: COGNITOHAZARDOUS INFLUENCE DETECTED.
groups.purpose: A small anomalous theater company that stages immersive productions using memetic and ontological anomalies.

groups.name: Sarkic Cults
lore: Overview: Sarkicism is a religious/philosophical system that encompasses a variety of traditions, beliefs, and spiritual practices largely based on teachings attributed to “Grand Karcist Ion”, its deified founder. Adherents practice ritual cannibalism, human sacrifice, corporeal augmentation, thaumaturgy, and dimensional manipulation. Highly secretive, the general public appears to have no direct knowledge of their existence; the one exception being the Church of the Broken God, who views them in apocalyptic terms. Organic manipulation has allowed certain Sarkicites to achieve anomalous states of being, transcending the physical limitations of baseline humans. Disease is viewed with reverence and Sarkic shrines have been discovered with offerings of swollen lymph nodes and tumorous growths. Sarkic cults treat contagions as consecration, a means to "cull the weak" and purify the masses, and thus actively seek to ensure their spread.

The Foundation divides known Sarkic cults into two distinct strands: Proto-Sarkic and Neo-Sarkic. Proto-Sarkic cults can be found in insular communities throughout Eurasia's most isolated regions, its followers generally poor (if self-reliant) and hostile towards outsiders. Such groups eschew modernity, display acute technophobia, and are bound by superstition and taboo. In contrast, Neo-Sarkic cults are cosmopolitan, publicly embracing modernity and showing no apparent qualms with technology; their public lives differing little from others of their culture and social status. Adherents are primarily affluent families, rich in history and scandal.

Ultimately, it is believed that the Foundation only knows a fraction of what Sarkicism is and what its followers intend. Based on the available information, the speculated goals of Sarkic cults represent an SK-class dominance shift, including the possibility of an XK-class end-of-the-world scenario.

The Hunter's Black Lodge is a criminal organization associated with a number of sarkic anomalies, collectively designated SCP-2408. Members of the crime syndicate are capable of anomalous physical transformations, and distribute substances with anomalous effects on both the mind and body. Although primarily active in states that were formerly part of the Soviet Union, the Hunter's Black Lodge has recently expanded its criminal activities into the United States.
