groups.name: The Serpent's Hand
lore: Overview: The Serpent's Hand is a small but formidable organization responsible for several security breaches. At least three different individuals have been encountered, all of whom used possible or confirmed anomalous items for infiltration purposes (including SCP-268, which was stolen from the Foundation, who had in turn recovered it during a raid of a Chaos Insurgency facility). The total number of members belonging to this organization is unknown, as is their level of technology, number of possible SCPs held, or total level of threat. However, it is clear they are highly coordinated and possibly dangerous. One of their leaders is thought to be a figure known as "L.S.", who is considered to be personally responsible for two security breaches in Foundation sites.

The Foundation currently has very little information about the Serpent's Hand, and almost all known information about the Serpent's Hand has been leaked from Global Occult Coalition intelligence. The group seems to embrace the use and existence of paranormal items, and in particular seems to embrace humanoid and sentient SCPs. The Serpent's Hand has been highly vocal in criticizing the containment and destruction of these SCPs, especially those which are fully human and are not particularly destructive.

The group seems to have unfriendly relations with the Chaos Insurgency and the ORIA, and an extremely hostile relationship with the Global Occult Coalition. The only recorded cases of unprovoked violence by Serpent's Hand members have been against Global Occult Coalition agents.

The Serpent's Hand seems primarily based in an anomalous location called the Wanderers' Library, a building accessed through portals found in many different parts of the world. Direct assaults on the Library have so far proven unfeasible, even when entrance could be found. However, initial intelligence seems to suggest the Hand has little understanding or control over the place.
Attempts to infiltrate the Wanderers' Library are ongoing.
groups.purpose: A small but formidable organization that embraces paranormal items, especially humanoid and sentient SCPs, and opposes their imprisonment.
groups.gear: Anomalous items used to infiltrate, including SCP-268, which was stolen from the Foundation. The brief says its overall level of technology is unknown.
gearQuotes: The total number of members belonging to this organization is unknown, as is their level of technology, number of possible SCPs held, or total level of threat.

groups.name: Shark Punching Center (SPC)
lore: Overview: The Shark Punching Center (also known as the Selachian Punching Center, The Shark Punching Centre, and Selachiosk Pungix Combin) is an organization located in one or more parallel universes, apparently acting as an alternate-universe counterpart to the Foundation. While the Foundation has known of the Center for several decades, the structure, documentation, and general tone taken by the Shark Punching Center varies wildly, suggesting one or more universes are in a state of flux.

Documents pertaining to the Shark Punching Center have been recovered, and indicate a much more militaristic and unstable tone than a Foundation document. As the name would suggest, the SPC is mostly focused on furthering hand-to-hand combat as a means to neutralize selachian entities, though some documentation fails to differentiate between "selachian" and "aquatic".
It is unclear if the Shark Punching Center has any knowledge or concern of or with Foundation activities.
groups.purpose: An alternate-universe counterpart to the Foundation, devoted to punching sharks.
groups.continuity: Its structure and documents vary wildly, which suggests its universes are in flux.

groups.name: Society of the Atheist Partisans of Progress for the Halt of the Irrational and Religious Enemy (SAPPHIRE)
lore: French Group of Interest Name: La Société Athée Pour la Halte de l'Idéologie Religieuse (SAPHIR)

Overview: The Society of the Atheist Partisans of Progress for the Halt of the Irrational and Religious Enemy, more commonly known by its acronym SAPPHIRE, is a group of extremist atheists largely present in Europe. Its adherents are, for the most part, members of the scientific community, belonging to an elusive international network. They regard SCP objects (which they call "Singularities") as a threat to scientific thinking and rationalism, by encouraging superstition and religious obscurantism. Their policy alternates between striving for the systematic destruction of SCP items, and using them as weapons to perpetrate acts of terrorism against religions, either in general or with a specific aim in mind.

SAPPHIRE’s attacks often indiscriminately target large numbers of civilians, forcing the Foundation to resort to extreme measures to conceal the anomalous means used from the public. Mobile Task Force Omega-5, "The Jewellers", has been created with the specific purpose of tracking, preventing or, in case of failure, covering up their attacks.

SAPPHIRE is in constant conflict with any and all form of cult, both ordinary and anomalous. They have numerous contacts in the scientific world, and some Foundation researchers have been revealed to be undercover affiliates of the group. Although SAPPHIRE generally respects the Foundation and its objectives, the group disapproves of the Foundation's policy of the preservation of SCP objects, and some of their spies have been captured after attempting to destroy or otherwise recover contained SCPs for their own personal interests.
Each and every undercover agent of SAPPHIRE must be reported, captured, and interrogated regarding the inner workings of the Society and their plans for future attacks.
groups.purpose: A group of extremist atheists, mostly scientists, that sees SCP objects ("Singularities") as a threat to scientific rationality. Translated from the French branch.
groups.gear: Sometimes uses SCP items as weapons for terrorism against religions.

groups.name: The Three Moons Initiative
lore: Overview: The Three Moons Initiative is an extradimensional human military organization based in SCP-2922-C, an afterlife also known as Corbenic. Through a partnership with the Corbenese deity JALAKÅRA, they act as a multi-dimensional security force for the protection of the human race.

While Initiative personnel believe that they're operating in humankind's best interests, military overreach, poor communication, issues with internal bureaucracy, and other factors — combined with their disproportionately high military strength to our own — have made them a potential liability to public safety in our dimension.
As such, they maintain an unstable peace with the Foundation. Operatives of the Three Moons Initiative are to be treated with extreme caution.
groups.purpose: An extradimensional human military based in the afterlife Corbenic (SCP-2922-C), acting as a multi-dimensional security force for humanity.
groups.gear: The brief describes military strength disproportionately high compared with our own, without detailing it.

groups.name: TotleighSoft
lore: Overview: TotleighSoft is a consumer electronics and software corporation based out of North Dakota. While TotleighSoft primarily produces anomalous video games, they have recently branched out into other fields such as home video and artificial intelligence.

The founder, CEO, and (arguably) sole employee is a gigantic extraterrestrial lifeform who answers to both SCP-2803-A and "P. Hudson Gock." Despite SCP-2803-A's immense reality-bending powers, it is nonetheless obsessed with the concept of the American Dream. To that end, it created TotleighSoft, becoming a self-proclaimed "immigarnt BUSNISS sucscsees sotry!!"

TotleighSoft's products are noted for their low quality, potent (and often harmful) anomalous qualities, and extremely poor spelling. However, the founder remains oblivious to these problems - not necessarily out of malice, but through stubborn naivete.

While also maintaining an uneasy relationship with TotleighSoft, the Foundation monitors, suppresses, and contains their products whenever we can. And yet, despite our best efforts, additional TotleighSoft content continues to reach the public through potentially anomalous means, garnering a sizable cult following over the years.
groups.purpose: A North Dakota electronics and software company run by a giant reality-bending extraterrestrial (SCP-2803-A), obsessed with the American Dream.

groups.name: Unusual Incidents Unit (UIU)
lore: Overview: The Unusual Incidents Unit of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI UIU) was formed after the onset of the Cold War, when many aspects of the American Government were focused on utilizing the anomalous and preventing the communists from doing the same. This led to the creation of a special FBI division devoted to rapid response to paranormal events and crimes. Director J. Edgar Hoover was personally involved with their creation.

Although initially given significant funding and resources by the American Government, following the end of the Cold War and the dissolution of enemy organizations such as the GRU-P, the UIU had been in a state of decline for many years.

Disparagingly referred to as "X-Files" and "UIUseless" by the larger anomalous community, the agency is generally well meaning, but due to a lack of financial resources, little manpower, and bureaucratic obstruction by the US Government, it is often perceived as ineffective. The influence of the Foundation and Global Occult Coalition in the United States Government has stopped the UIU and other USGOV entities dealing with anomalous activity, such as US Air Force's 616th Squadron ("Roswell's Revengers") and US Navy SEAL Team Bravo Papa Romeo Delta, from being dissolved entirely.

FBI Agents and Special Agents who join the Unusual Incidents Unit often have backgrounds in psychology, STEM fields, and art studies. As part of the PATRIOT act, agents of the unit are required to be administered Personalized Memetic Silencing Agents (PMSA, colloquially referred to as 'gag orders' by agents of the UIU) to avoid leaks.

The Unusual Incidents Unit has been known to engage in combat alongside and against various anomalous organizations in the past, including participating in several combat operations under Foundation supervision in the 1950s and 1960s, and the "Black Mamba" incident in Afghanistan in 1976, an infamous skirmish between UIU agents and members of GRU-P.

Currently, a division of the Unusual Incidents Unit oversees the autonomous anomalous state of Three Portlands. An example of underfunding and understaffing in the Unusual Incidents Unit can be seen in its sole remaining division in the Midwestern United States.
groups.purpose: An FBI division formed after the start of the Cold War for rapid response to paranormal events and crimes.
groups.continuity: Its funding and standing change considerably across its history and in different tales.

groups.name: Valravn Corporation
lore: Overview: The Valravn Corporation is an Anomalous Private Military Company, mostly operating in politically unstable regions where the presence of organizations like the Foundation and the Global Occult Coalition is less prominent. They are mainly hired by governments to suppress anomalous rebel groups and protect their interest against otherworldly threats.

Valravn sells itself as a specialist in "anomalous security and counter-insurgency". It specializes in the weaponization of myth-related anomalies as well as paratechnologically augmented soldiers. The origins of the Valravn Corporation can be traced back to the fall of the legendary mercenary Jomsviking order and it is believed to have existed throughout history in various iterations. Valravn professes a syncretic belief in pagan Norse determinism combined with hyper-capitalism worship, which it uses to ideologically justify its mercenary business.

Their relationship with the Foundation is tense, with an unstable peace maintained as long as Valravn commits to operating under the Veil. However, Valravn's ongoing conflict with the Serpent's Hand splinter cell, Las Víboras, has complicated this agreement.

lore: Overview: Here at Vikander-Kneed we like to pride ourselves on being at the bleeding edge of media and communications technology. Our goal has been the betterment of the person and society through unbiased but aesthetically pleasing communications.
If there’s a better world out there, then it’s up to all of us to achieve it together. Efficient and entertaining media is the most important step on the road to Utopia.
Won’t you join us in this Better Tomorrow TM?

groups.name: The Wandsmen
lore: Overview: The Wandsmen are a group of extradimensional journalists and archivists. They seek to explore the multiverse and uncover its mysteries, while spreading and preserving knowledge.

All members of this group undergo a transformation that gives them avian features and anomalous abilities. They also utilize a group of anomalous artifacts known as "Maps of the Multiverse" to travel through dimensions to study their locales and inhabitants.

In contrast to many groups of interest, the Wandsmen have attempted to work with the Foundation multiple times. One of their goals is the preservation of existence so they can study it, so they see the Foundation as an ally against the multiverse's destruction.

However, they have a variety of extremely dangerous members, have produced multiple anomalous items, and strongly object philosophically to the Foundation's desire to preserve normalcy and conceal knowledge of the anomalous.

groups.name: Wilson's Wildlife Solutions
lore: Overview: Wilson's Wildlife Solutions is a paranormal publicly funded wildlife service based in Clackamas County, Oregon, specifically in the town of Boring. Although the Foundation has known of Wilson's Wildlife Solutions' existence and anomalous affiliations since 1999, it took nine years until the Ursus Maritimus Incident in 2008, for their existence to be officially recognized and a relationship established between the two groups. Currently the Boring Agreement outlines that Wilson's Wildlife Solutions should be supervised by MTF Beta-4 ("Castaways"), local to Site-64, and that they may handle containment of Safe or Euclid fauna based anomalies with varying degrees of Foundation intervention (on a case to case basis). Amendments to the Boring Agreement can be, and have been, made to account for grey areas or new policies as necessary.
groups.purpose: A publicly funded paranormal wildlife service in Boring, Oregon, working with the Foundation under the Boring Agreement.

groups.name: American Secure Containment Initiative (ASCI)
lore: Overview: The American Secure Containment Initiative (ASCI) was one of a number of anomaly containment organisations that merged together to establish the modern Foundation. While it existed, ASCI was the primary paranormal agency of the United States of America, containing or neutralizing anomalies and concealing their existence from the American public. Unlike the Foundation, ASCI was also tasked with using anomalies to advance American interests both domestically and abroad, a role that has now been taken on by the Pentagram.

The Foundation inherited multiple anomalies from this precursor organization, as well as facilities still in use today, including Site-55, Site-88 and Area-14. The American Secure Containment Initiative also developed methods still in use by the modern Foundation, including diplomatic engagement with the inhabited anomalous communities now classified as Nexuses, as well as the recruitment of D-class personnel. While primarily of historical interest, ASCI records can provide important context for the current practices of the Foundation.
groups.purpose: A Foundation precursor that served as the United States' paranormal agency. It also used anomalies to advance American interests.

groups.name: British Occult Service
lore: Overview: The British Occult Service, also known as the Royal Occult Service, is the United Kingdom's primary paranormal intelligence agency. As the occult counterpart to MI5 and MI6, it is known colloquially as "MI13" or "MI666". While the current organization is a relatively modern creation, it traces its origin back to a long line of spies, magicians and alchemists who have been part of royal retinues throughout British history. The chief of the British Occult Service is known only as "D", in reference to the occultist John Dee, who served Queen Elizabeth I.

Once operating throughout the British Empire, the independence of former British colonies dramatically decreased the organization's global reach over the course of the 20th Century. As a founding member of the Allied Occult Initiative, the British Occult Service retains a permanent seat on the Global Occult Coalition's Council of 108, and this is now the main means through which it exerts international influence. Domestically, the British Occult Service gathers intelligence on British subjects through both mundane methods and clairvoyance, detaining threats to normalcy using a special paranormal division of the Metropolitan Police Force.

The British Occult Service answers directly to the Crown, lacking any formal Parliamentary oversight. This grants it a great deal of autonomy to pursue British interests, both within the United Kingdom and abroad. Historic ties between HMFSCP and the British Occult Service mean that conflict with the Foundation is infrequent, as continued cooperation enables both organizations to operate covertly in the United Kingdom, without interference from the general public or their elected representatives.
groups.purpose: The UK's paranormal intelligence agency ("MI13"), descended from royal spies, magicians and alchemists.

groups.name: Japan Organisms Improvement and Creation Laboratory (JOICL)
lore: Japanese Group of Interest Name: 日本生類創研

Overview: Japan Organisms Improvement and Creation Laboratory (JOICL) has been connected to a wide range of life forms, including animals, plants and objects which behave like living organisms. Almost all of these entities exhibit anomalous properties that cannot be observed in nature or explained by conventional science, and the laboratory's research does not appear to be restricted by either physical laws or ethical principles. JOICL is thought to be a research facility or group of researchers with access to some kind of anomalous technology, but its exact nature and capabilities are currently unknown.

Initially it was thought that there was no direct distribution or sale of the anomalies created by the Japan Organisms Improvement and Creation Laboratory, but in rare cases the organization has been confirmed to sell their creations as commercial products, including SCP-483-JP or SCP-1919-JP. Its organizational purpose remains unknown.

groups.name: OBSKURA
lore: Overview: The Obskurakorps were the occult arm of the Nazi Ahnenerbe, placing occultists recruited from the Thule Society under the command of the SS. Initially tasked with research intended to prove Aryan racial superiority, their efforts to weaponize anomalies during the Second World War lead to the 7th Occult War, in which the Obskurakorps were opposed and eventually defeated by the combined efforts of the Allied Occult Initiative and the Foundation.

After the conclusion of the war, most surviving members of the Obskurakorps were detained or executed by the recently established Global Occult Coalition. Some former members were recruited by organizations including the Foundation and the Pentagram, while others were amnestized and returned to civilian life. A small number evaded capture through the aid of an organization known as OBSKURA, which transported them to the Middle East and South America. This network persisted, developing into a neo-Nazi organization lead by a self-proclaimed Führer, claiming to be the successor to Adolf Hitler.

Both the Foundation and the Global Occult Coalition continue to oppose OBSKURA. While the organization lacks any official government backing, it has operatives trained in thaumaturgy, and retains a number of paranormal artifacts, acquired during the war and then smuggled out of Europe by OBSKURA. While it mostly tries to spread its Nazi ideology in secret, its members do not hesitate to use their anomalous capabilities against their foes.

groups.name: PENTAGRAM
lore: Overview: The United States Paranatural Warfare Command, usually known simply as the Pentagram, is the division of the Department of Defense responsible for paranormal operations and intelligence. The Pentagram counters anomalous threats to the United States of America and its interests abroad, through both covert operations and the development and use of paranormal weapons.

Although the Pentagram was a member of the Allied Occult Initiative during the 7th Occult War, the Pentagram only cooperates with the Foundation and Global Occult Coalition to the extent that this is advantageous to their own military objectives. Their paranormal arms race with the GRU Division "P" contributed to the escalation of tensions during the Cold War, and after the fall of the Soviet Union the Pentagram has shifted its focus to contemporary US adversaries, including extensive involvement in the War on Terror. Assets under their command include the Navy's 13th Fleet, SEAL Team Bravo Papa Romeo Delta, the Air Force's 616th Squadron ("Roswell's Revengers"), and the Army's 23rd Paranatural Operations Group.

The secrecy required for its anomalous operations shields the Pentagram from civilian oversight, and the organization answers directly to the President of the United States. On multiple occasions, the Pentagram's development and deployment of anomalous assets has threatened to reveal the existence of the anomalous to the general public, necessitating extensive cover-up operations. While the Foundation generally avoids antagonizing the USA through direct opposition to the Pentagram, on rare occasions this has been necessary to ensure that certain anomalies do not fall into their hands.
